title: Build Data Source and Destination Providers
readerIntent: Integrate SFTP, object storage, HTTPS, partner APIs, enterprise gateways, or delivery systems safely.
priorKnowledge: Know the import remote-source or export destination contract.
owner: Reusable provider or customer-project adapter module
summary: Providers resolve named configuration, stage or deliver bounded data, and return normalized evidence; they never accept arbitrary request credentials or bypass the shared lifecycle.

sections.heading: Import source provider
items: Register named sources and transports in layered configuration.
Resolve credentials through secret governance.
Enforce tenant/module allowlists, timeouts, retries, count, size, extension, and checksum policy.
Stage files into an isolated server-owned location.
Return trusted references to the normal import lifecycle and clean up according to policy.

sections.heading: Export destination provider
items: Register governed destination aliases and capabilities.
Accept normalized streams or batches from the shared export engine.
Enforce path/key constraints, encryption, checksums, retries, idempotency, retention, and cleanup.
Return normalized delivery evidence without exposing provider secrets.

sections.heading: Qualification
items: Invalid configuration and secret handling.
Tenant isolation and source/destination authorization.
Timeout, retry, duplicate, partial transfer, resume, cleanup, and shutdown.
Live provider compatibility, limits, performance, outage, recovery, security, and upgrade.

sections.heading: Customize and extend safely
paragraphs: An import provider parses and normalizes; it does not own business validation or persistence. An export provider renders or delivers already authorized data; it does not choose unrestricted fields.
Business modules and generic data-exchange services remain unchanged when a provider is added.

sections.heading: Configuration and secrets
items: Stable provider type and supported modes.
Encoding, delimiter, sheet, mapping, compression, and size options.
Destination aliases, endpoints, TLS, and secret references.
Timeout, retry, concurrency, batching, and cleanup.
Explicit capability and limitation flags.

sections.heading: Failure and lifecycle
items: Reject malformed or unsupported input safely.
Bound parsing and rendering resources.
Preserve record and destination error context without payload leakage.
Retry only idempotent reads or writes.
Clean temporary resources and close connections.
Support restart and resume where claimed.

sections.heading: Release evidence
items: Contract and format compatibility.
Boundary, malicious, malformed, and large inputs.
Credential, tenant, field, and destination isolation.
Partial source or destination failure.
Load, recovery, upgrade, and rollback.
Beginner configuration and operator runbooks.
